destination.name: Myall Lakes National Park
destination.tagline: A coastal park of beaches, dunes and one of the state's largest lake systems, north of Port Stephens.
destination.description: Myall Lakes National Park covers 448 square kilometres of lakes, 40 km of beaches and rolling sand dunes, and includes Broughton Island. The fishing village of Seal Rocks sits on its coast beside Sugarloaf Point Lighthouse, a tower with an external stairway built in 1875. Walks run from rainforest headlands to Dark Point, a Worimi gathering place for at least 4,000 years. It is one of the most visited parks in New South Wales.
whyVisit: See Sugarloaf Point Lighthouse above Seal Rocks
Spend a day on Seal Rocks' beaches
Walk Treachery Headland to lighthouse views

goodToKnow.title: Drive in; entry fees apply
goodToKnow.detail: There are no buses into the park, and a per-vehicle entry fee applies. Check the NPWS page for current prices.

goodToKnow.title: Mind the Bombah Point ferry
goodToKnow.detail: The quickest route from the Pacific Highway uses a cable ferry across Two Mile Lake, so allow for it. Seal Rocks Road avoids the ferry.

goodToKnow.title: Respect Dark Point
goodToKnow.detail: Dark Point is a sacred Worimi place. 4WDs are allowed on the beach near it only under conditions, so stay on marked tracks.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Beaches and lakes are at their best in {months}; whale-watching from the dunes and headlands runs May to November instead.
